points.quote: Edgeless mode doesn't store a separate copy of the document. It adds data to the same Yjs doc that page mode uses.
The `affine:surface` block is the page's second child. It is the edgeless layer, and its schema declares `parent: ['@root']`.
Shapes, brush strokes, highlighter strokes, connectors, groups, mindmaps and canvas text are not blocks. They live inside the surface block's single `elements` prop.
Each `affine:note` block ... also carries edgeless props: `xywh`, `index` ... This is how a note appears as a card on the canvas.

A note's `displayMode` controls where it shows. It can be edgeless-only, or visible in both the doc and edgeless views. / Rich objects are real child blocks of the surface: `affine:frame`, `affine:image`...
every element and every edgeless block has `xywh`. It is a serialized string such as "[x,y,w,h]".
each element and block has a fractional-indexing string in `index`, generated with `generateKeyBetween`... sorts by this string to produce the z-order.
a `group` element ... has a `children` prop that is a `Y.Map<boolean>` of child id -> `true` ... the group's bounds come from them.
